summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 10, part 145) in which an envoy named Leon meets Ria, a woman of about 40 with iron-grey hair who is the central figure of the place called Ate, in a sensory room called the Living Room. They shake hands, Ria invites him to go barefoot, and the two share a laugh over the room's design and whether anyone has ever snuck in to screw something onto the furnishings. The scene is playful and sensory, with the moss floor and topiary chairs prominent, and ends with Ria urging them to get to it.
one_line: Envoy Leon meets Ria, the central figure of Ate, in the sensory Living Room, where they go barefoot and share a laugh.
key_facts: Leon is an envoy who is out of place in Ate, though Ria does not hold it against him.
Ria is the center of the whole business and the soul of Ate.
Leon estimates Ria's age at around 40.
Ria is described as hippy, a little wrinkled, with iron-grey hair brushed off her face.
Ria introduces herself to Leon with the words "Call me Ria."
Ria sits cross-legged on a topiary chair after kicking off her hush puppies.
Ria tells Leon, "I love this room!" and calls the room "Fantastic."
Leon kicks off his handmade shoes, which were designed by an architect who had given up on literary criticism to pursue cobblery.
The floor of the Living Room feels perfect to Leon, and he cannot pin down whether it is warm or cool.
Ria says, "I'm thinking something that goes straight into the nerves," and calls it extraordinary.
Ria remarks that the room was clearly designed to impress and that she is impressed.
Ria wonders aloud whether anyone has ever snuck into the Living Room and screwed on that stuff.
Leon sits down on the mossy floor, letting it brush his feet, ankles, palms and wrists.
Leon says, "If no one ever has, it's a damned shame," with mock gravity.
Ria ends the exchange by saying, "Let's get to it," and does not want to waste time.
